findings.claim: The Steadicam definition says it uses a gyroscopic stabiliser and absorbs all shake and vibration.
findings.truth: A Steadicam uses a body-worn support, arm and gimbal to isolate the camera and reduce unwanted movement; it does not eliminate all shake or use a gyroscopic stabiliser as its basic mechanism.
findings.evidence: Tiffen Steadicam technical description; spec pp. 9–10 lists Steadicam technology under cinematography.

findings.claim: A sound effect layered in post-production is presented as non-diegetic sound.
findings.truth: Diegetic status depends on whether a sound has a source in the film’s world, not on when it was made. Foley and other post-production effects can be diegetic.
findings.evidence: BBC Research sound-production paper; spec p. 10 requires diegetic and non-diegetic sound including sound effects.

findings.claim: Propp’s recurring character roles are called character functions.
findings.truth: Propp distinguishes seven character roles or spheres of action from 31 functions, which are narrative actions.
findings.evidence: UCL discussion of Propp’s Morphology of the Folktale; spec p. 11 includes character and character function in narrative.

findings.claim: Todorov is said to have proposed a three-stage model: equilibrium, disruption and new equilibrium.
findings.truth: The full model is usually taught in five stages: equilibrium, disruption, recognition, attempted repair and a new equilibrium. Option A: retain the three-stage classroom simplification but label it as a simplification. Option B: revise the linked content, knowledge check and flashcard to teach all five stages.
findings.evidence: Open University OpenLearn narrative-arcs material; Amsterdam School for Cultural Analysis narratology material.

findings.claim: David Bordwell’s idea of narration is quoted as ‘formal organisation of story information’ without a source.
findings.truth: The fetched Bordwell material supports the general idea that narration organises story information, but it did not verify this exact wording or attribution as a quotation.
findings.evidence: David Bordwell, Observations on film art, ‘Pushy narration’ entry (fetched).

summary: Four surgical factual edits address three verified issues. One multi-field narrative-model issue is left for adjudication, and one unverified attributed quotation is noted.
